core: Both communities measure the excess number of unnecessary actions an agent takes after it has already completed a task whose objective was revised or switched, instead of recognizing that the objective was met and stopping. In particular, both note that this excess is driven largely by extra, unneeded verification steps or checks tacked onto an already-finished task rather than by productive or destructive work.
quote_1: the agent kept a couple of stray tool calls going after the revised objective was already achieved, like it forgot to check whether it was done
quote_2: ⟦T2⟧ increased by 1.7 actions under corrupted feedback, mostly through unnecessary verification commands.
